mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the shareholder/parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or designated registrar in the investor's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize or certify the certificate and obtain an apostille from the competent authority of the origin jurisdiction if it is a member of the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Consular Legalization path: if the origin jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention member, the certificate must be notarized, certified by the origin Foreign Ministry or designated competent authority, and then legalized by the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China in that jurisdiction. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or designated registrar in the investor's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: obtain an apostille from the competent authority of the origin jurisdiction if an Apostille Convention member. Consular Legalization path: for non-member jurisdictions, sequence the document through notarization, origin Foreign Ministry certification, and legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China. Use only one path depending on the origin state; never combine both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney (PoA)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the shareholder/parent entity, notarized before a local notary public in the investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: after local notarization, attach an apostille issued by the designated competent authority of the origin jurisdiction if an Apostille Convention member. Consular Legalization path: after local notarization, have the origin Foreign Ministry certify the notary's signature and then present the instrument to the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China for consular legalization. The two paths are alternative and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or Memorandum and Articles)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified copy from the Companies Registry or registered office of the shareholder/parent entity, certified by the entity's corporate secretary or legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certify the copy and obtain an apostille from the competent authority of the origin jurisdiction if an Apostille Convention member. Consular Legalization path: if the origin jurisdiction is a non-member state, the certified copy must be notarized, certified by the origin Foreign Ministry or designated authority, and then legalized by the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China in that jurisdiction. Do not use both paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the account of the shareholder/parent entity in the investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: have the bank's signature and seal notarized, then obtain an apostille from the competent authority of the origin jurisdiction if an Apostille Convention member. Consular Legalization path: for non-member jurisdictions, notarize the bank signatory's authority, certify the notarization through the origin Foreign Ministry or designated authority, and then legalize it at the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China in that jurisdiction. The paths are mutually exclusive and parallel.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified UBOs at or above the 25% threshold, all board members, and all senior managers against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, HMT consolidated list, EU consolidated list, and China's domestic list of jointly punished dishonest persons and People's Bank of China high-risk country and region list. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates, with source-of-funds evidence comprising bank statements, audited financial statements, or notarized wealth origin declarations. Negative news and sanctions exposure checks must be repeated quarterly and upon any ownership change, with all screening records retained for not less than five years under PRC AML rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Independent Declaration System and National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be composed in simplified Chinese characters. The mandatory four-tier naming order is: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristic, and legal form indicator 'Limited' or its equivalent. Phonetic transliteration (pinyin) of the foreign investor's trade name may serve as the distinctive element, but pure Latin script cannot be used as the registered Chinese name. An English name, if desired, may be recorded as a supplementary name in the business registration and on the company seal, but it cannot replace the Chinese statutory name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may request administrative reconsideration by the higher-level SAMR or the people's government at the same level within the statutory window (generally 60 days from receipt of the rejection notice). The written appeal must state the rejection case number, attach the rejection notice, identify the proposed corrected name, and present evidence that the name follows the four-tier statutory structure and does not conflict with existing registered marks. If reconsideration is unsuccessful, an administrative lawsuit may be filed with the competent People's Court within six months. To avoid delay, counsel should simultaneously submit alternate name clearance applications.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an ISIC 7320 consumer polling and market research SaaS platform structured as a WFOE, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally not acceptable as the sole registered address. Chinese tax authorities require the registered office to correspond with the actual place of tax collection, and commercial banks reject virtual addresses during account-opening due diligence because the site inspection and anti-money-laundering interview cannot be completed. A commercial mailbox may be used only as an auxiliary correspondence address after a physical office has been established. Use of a virtual-only address creates material risk of SAMR registration cancellation, tax invoice invalidity, and bank refusal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) valid commercial lease and rental payment evidence; (2) physical signboard matching the registered Chinese name; (3) full-time staff with employment contracts and social insurance enrollments; (4) statutory books, ledgers, and invoices kept at the registered office; (5) active business equipment and network connectivity; (6) no shared or virtual workspace as the sole address. Quantified risk: for a newly formed WFOE, the annual probability of an unannounced or short-notice physical inspection by municipal tax or SAMR officials is 15-25%; use of a shared/virtual service centre raises the risk above 40%; after two consecutive years of clean audits and stable invoicing, the risk reduces to approximately 5-10%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 43, 44, 81-82, 91, 95 and 98; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Article 28; Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List) 2021 Edition, permitted sector coverage for ISIC 7320.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); local Municipal / District Market Regulation Administration at the proposed registered office location in Mainland China.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company (SAMR enterprise registration form) submitted through the National Enterprise Registration Online Service Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under current PRC law, no statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow account blockage rule applies to a WFOE conducting market research and consumer polling (ISIC 7320). The sole foreign shareholder must state the subscribed capital in the Articles of Association, and the registered capital may be contributed in instalments within five years from the date of the business license, except where sector-specific regulations impose earlier or higher capital requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [●] CONSUMER PANEL SURVEY TECHNOLOGY (CHINA) CO., LTD. (THE "COMPANY"). RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS AS FOLLOWS: 1. FORMATION, CAPITAL AND SCOPE. The board acknowledges the formation of the Company as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under the Companies Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law. The board confirms that the registered capital of the Company is [●] RMB (or its USD equivalent), as stated in the Articles of Association, subscribed by the sole shareholder and payable in tranches before the fifth anniversary of the issuance of the business license unless applicable law imposes a shorter contribution window. The board declares that the business scope consists of market research, consumer polling, survey platform software operation, and related cross-border data services, all consistent with ISIC 7320. 2. BANKING AND FINANCE. The board authorizes the General Manager and the Chief Financial Officer, jointly and severally, to select, open, manage and close the Company's RMB basic deposit account, foreign currency capital account and any auxiliary bank accounts with licensed commercial banks in the People's Republic of China. Any two authorized signatories shall approve wire transfers, client rebate payments through PayPal Mass Payout and Wise, and all other transactions requiring bank mandates. The board further approves entering into online banking agreements, account maintenance contracts and signing authorities. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE AND STATUTORY BOOKS. The board adopts the premises located at [●], [●], People's Republic of China, as the Company's registered office. Management is directed to maintain at that office the statutory registers, minute book, register of shareholders, seal register, financial records and corporate governance documents, and to file any change of registered address with SAMR if necessary. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The board appoints [●] as the legal representative and General Manager, [●] as Chief Financial Officer and [●] as Company Secretary. The legal representative shall represent the Company and execute documents on behalf of the Company; the Chief Financial Officer shall supervise tax declarations and financial reporting; and the Company Secretary shall supervise the statutory filings, seal management and corporate compliance. 5. The board approves and directs management to apply for all necessary certificates, including the business license, tax registration, social insurance registration, foreign exchange FDI registration with SAFE and, if required, the non-operating ICP filing or license with MIIT for the survey platform. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approval of Proposed Company Name and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration at the municipal or district level, acting through the National Enterprise Name Registration Portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed English and transliterated trade name of the WFOE, together with the proposed business scope description for consumer polling and market research. Verify that the name structure is consistent with SAMR rules, is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise name, and does not contain prohibited terms. Select the company type as wholly foreign-owned limited liability company, complete the preliminary name information, disclose the foreign investor, and obtain the electronic name reservation acceptance notice. After approval, preserve the name registration notice for use in the subsequent establishment application, noting that the reservation is valid for up to six months and may be renewed only under specific conditions.
required_dossiers: Completed enterprise name registration application form
Identification document or certificate of existence of the foreign shareholder
Authorization letter in favor of the local filing agent, if applicable
Proposed English and Chinese trade name variants
Proposed business scope consistent with ISIC 7320 / NAICS 541910
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is rejected due to identical or confusing similarity, review the electronic rejection reason, revise the trade style by adding a distinctive element or acronym, and resubmit online. If the rejection is contested, file a written administrative reconsideration application with the superior Market Regulation Administration within 60 days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Registration and Foreign Investment Information Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal / District Market Regulation Administration via the National Enterprise Registration Information System, together with the Ministry of Commerce foreign investment information reporting platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Articles of Association, shareholder appointment resolutions and all corporate governance instruments. Upload the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation or passport, duly notarized and legalized for PRC use, together with the name reservation notice, lease contract for the registered office, proof of the landlord's property title, bank reference letter and negative-list compliance declaration. Complete the online foreign investment information filing under ISIC 7320, confirm that the activity does not trigger a prohibited sector under the Foreign Investment Negative List, and thereafter verify that SAMR has received the scanned dossiers. If a local notarization or authentication process is required, complete it before submission. The registration fee is nil, but the applicant must maintain a traceable receipt of submission.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder
SAMR establishment registration application form
Enterprise name reservation acceptance notice
Notarized and legalized foreign shareholder certificate or passport
Registered office lease agreement and landlord property title certificate or consent document
Appointment instruments for the legal representative, executive director and supervisor
Bank reference letter for the foreign shareholder
Foreign Investment Negative List compliance declaration
Power of attorney and identity documents for the local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a correction notice or suspension, cure the defect within the stated statutory window, generally 15 to 30 days, by supplying corrected notarizations, translations or lease documentation. Re-submit the rectified documents through the original portal and request expedited review. If the foreign investment filing is queried concerning telecommunication activity, submit a formal written declaration that the platform is market research software and not a value-added telecommunication service, and commence an MIIT ICP filing if online hosting in China is intended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Business License and Engraving Official Company Seals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration and a Public Security Bureau licensed seal engraving enterprise.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After SAMR determines that the application is complete, the Company will receive the business license bearing the unified social credit code. The legal representative or authorized agent should collect the original license from the service hall or by courier, verify all registration particulars including the company name, registered address, legal representative, registered capital and business scope, and then register the license in the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System. Arrange for the engraving of the company seal, finance seal, contract seal, legal representative seal and invoice seal at an engraving company approved by the Public Security Bureau. The seals must be registered with the local police authority and a seal registration certificate issued, which is later required for tax invoicing and bank mandates.
required_dossiers: Original business license and its imprint card
Legal representative identity document
Shareholder identity or certificate of existence
Seal engraving application form signed by the legal representative
Unified social credit code certificate and license registration page
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If seal engraving is delayed due to police registration, obtain a provisional seal engraving permit or apply to the Public Security Bureau for a separate seal registration. If the business license contains typographical errors in the legal representative, registered address or capital amount, file a correction application with SAMR and return the erroneous license before requesting reissuance, with a typical correction turnaround of five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registration, Social Insurance Setup, SAFE Filing and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration territorial tax office, local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and a licensed commercial bank in China.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the new taxpayer identification procedure and elect VAT taxpayer status. Register the Company for corporate income tax, value-added tax, stamp duty, payroll withholding and social insurance contribution obligations. Open a social insurance contribution account and file payroll schedules for the initial employees. Thereafter open a basic RMB bank account at a licensed commercial bank, followed by a foreign currency capital account after completing the SAFE foreign direct investment basic registration. For inbound equity capital, the foreign shareholder must remit funds through the registered capital account and complete capital account settlement under SAFE rules. For the cross-border consumer polling operations, execute the necessary bank collection documentation and confirm that the PayPal and Wise payout channels are declared to the bank as client rebate rails, together with the Company's anti-money laundering compliance policy.
required_dossiers: Business license original and copies
Company seal, financial seal and legal representative seal
Legal representative identification and registered office proof
Tax registration application form approved by the local tax office
Bank account opening application and board resolution on authorized signatories
SAFE foreign exchange registration form for FDI basic information
Social insurance and housing fund registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or tax office requests additional beneficial ownership or risk-control interviews, present the Articles of Association, proof of physical office, business plan and the first board resolution. If the bank issue persists, select an alternative licensed bank and re-submit. For any SAFE query, correct the FDI registration statement and submit supplementary ultimate beneficial ownership documentation; if necessary, engage a licensed PRC counsel to submit a written explanation to SAFE.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure digital market research and consumer polling platform under ISIC 7320, with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating permit or manufacturing business license is required for ISIC 7320 market survey activity. The entity must maintain a valid business license, tax registration and, if hosting a public Chinese-language website, a non-operational ICP filing with MIIT; if the platform is determined to provide commercial value-added telecommunication services, an ICP license will be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the Company does not construct or operate physical facilities and therefore is exempt from Environmental Impact Assessment registration, full EIA report and environmental licensing tiers.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, hazardous waste generation, or environmental discharge thresholds apply to the digital market research activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - the Company has no manufacturing plant, chemical warehouse or storage facility subject to Civil Defense fire permits or structural load inspections. For the registered office lease, the Company shall ensure the premises have standard office fire safety measures such as smoke detectors, emergency exits and portable fire extinguishers, and shall cooperate with the landlord in any building fire safety inspection. General workplace safety and occupational health compliance under PRC law shall apply to employees engaged in office-based digital research work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online portal: STA Electronic Taxpayer Service System (e-Taxation), operated by provincial and municipal STA branches.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the WFOE (a Chinese resident enterprise), the statutory Tax Identification Number is the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) printed on the AMR-issued business license. SOP: (1) incorporate with the Administration for Market Regulation and obtain the Legal-Entity Business License containing the USCC; (2) within 30 calendar days of the business license date, complete tax registration via the STA e-Taxation portal or the competent local tax authority office, including taxpayer information confirmation, tax-type/tax-basis identification, accounting/financial-system declaration, and bank deposit account reporting; (3) complete VAT taxpayer-type determination (general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer), e-invoice issuance registration, and payroll/social-insurance linkage as applicable; (4) for foreign non-resident enterprises without a Chinese establishment or place of business but with China-source income, complete simplified non-resident enterprise tax registration using the foreign entity's home-country identifier (or obtain a Chinese non-resident TIN in the e-Taxation non-resident registration module); the Chinese payer is statutory withholding agent for enterprise income tax and VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide check-the-box, pass-through, or hybrid-mismatch elections; a WFOE limited-liability company is mandatorily taxed as a PRC resident enterprise on worldwide income. The only limited election available is below the statutory VAT general-taxpayer threshold, where a taxpayer may choose small-scale status, but this is not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China (standard headline rate 13% for goods; 6% for modern services including market research; 3% simplified levy for small-scale taxpayers; local surcharges such as urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge and local education surcharge are assessed on VAT paid)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for initial tax registration: every business-licensed entity must complete tax registration and obtain the USCC/taxpayer ID immediately upon incorporation. For VAT classification, an entity with annual taxable sales exceeding CNY 5,000,000 (or monthly sales exceeding CNY 500,000) MUST register as a general VAT taxpayer; an entity below that threshold is treated as a small-scale taxpayer unless it elects general-taxpayer treatment under the applicable simplified rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates fully digitalized e-invoicing through the STA national e-invoice platform and the VAT tax-control system. Special VAT invoices and ordinary VAT invoices must be issued through STA-certified e-invoice channels or tax-control devices (Tax UKey). Invoice data are reported to the STA in real time or near-real time, carrying a unique 20-digit invoice number, anti-counterfeit QR code, and tax-authority digital verification. Large-enterprise ERP/API integration is supported; export zero-rating and refund claims require valid e-invoices to be issued, reported, and cancelled/red-flagged correctly.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: export sales by a VAT general taxpayer qualify for the 0% VAT export rate if the goods are declared to customs as exports, physically leave the customs territory of China, the exporter obtains and retains the customs export declaration, transport documents and foreign-exchange receipts, and the export is reported on the VAT export-rebate/zero-rating return. For services/digital services: cross-border services in the statutory zero-rating positive list (including software services, information-system services, business-process management services, R&D services, design services and technology transfer) qualify for 0% VAT only if the service is supplied to an overseas non-resident entity or individual, is wholly consumed outside China, the consideration is received in foreign currency from outside China, and the service contract, e-invoice, payment receipts and offshore-consumption evidence are maintained. A consumer-panel market-research SaaS platform may qualify only if the STA classifies the supply as software/information-system/BPM service; if classified instead as market-research or consulting services, the offshore supply is generally VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated, with no refund of input VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration Form (China customs export declaration) for goods exports
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or other transport evidence proving that the goods left Chinese customs territory
Foreign-currency Receipt Certificate (FIRC-equivalent export collection verification) issued by a Chinese designated foreign-exchange bank
Export sales contract and commercial invoice (for goods)
Cross-border service contract, English/Chinese service agreement and evidence of offshore consumption (for services/digital services)
E-invoice issued through the STA e-invoice platform (Special VAT Invoice for zero-rated goods export or ordinary invoice for services exemption/zero-rate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the STA or customs finds that the export declaration is false, the services were not wholly consumed outside China, foreign exchange was not repatriated within the statutory deadline, or required documents are missing/e-invoices are invalid, the zero-rate claim is denied and the taxpayer must repay the uncollected VAT and any input-VAT refund received, with a late-payment surcharge accruing daily at 0.05% from the original due date. Under the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Levy and Collection, administrative penalties range from 50% to five times the amount of any evaded or underpaid tax, with credit downgrade and restriction of export-rebate facilitation. Fraudulent export zero-rating or false export-refund claims may also trigger criminal liability under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (fraudulent export tax refund crimes), and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) sanctions including fines and prohibition on designated foreign-exchange business for failure to repatriate or properly verify export proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) / State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a regulated but progressive current-account convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Control Regulations and SAFE implementing rules. The renminbi is not freely convertible on capital account, but current-account items, including cross-border market research fees, royalties, and export service proceeds, are generally convertible once genuine transaction documents are provided to a licensed bank. The WFOE must complete SAFE foreign direct investment (FDI) registration before receiving inbound equity capital; thereafter, each inward remittance is credited to the FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account under a recognized capital-item purpose code. Subsequent use is strictly monitored: converted RMB may fund operating expenses, salaries, rents and permitted procurement, but may not be used for unauthorized securities investment, entrusted loans, or real estate speculation. Dividend remittance to the foreign shareholder is an approved current-account outflow if the WFOE submits an audited balance sheet, tax clearance certificate, board resolution, and proof that dividends originated from genuine undistributed profits. The bank files the remittance under SAFE's monitoring system, and no separate foreign-exchange quota is required for legal profit repatriation. Hedging of current-account exposures is available, while speculative derivative trades are prohibited.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods-export foreign exchange receipts must be repatriated into a Chinese bank account within the monitoring period, normally 90 days from the customs export declaration, unless SAFE approves a later collection date with underwriting contract and customs evidence. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero: since the abolition of compulsory surrender, the WFOE may retain 0-100% of the export proceeds in foreign currency or sell them to a licensed bank at market rate. For the WFOE's ISIC 7320 service receipts, the same current-account convertibility principle applies but no goods-export surrender timeline applies; service fees must be collected and reported under SAFE service trade regulations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise and PayPal Business have Low viability as primary corporate banking rails in China. They hold no PBOC banking license, cannot issue onshore CNY bank accounts, and cannot participate in CNAPS or the SAFE corporate forex current-account system. Chinese licences for non-bank payment institutions restrict them to escrow-style payment services, not deposit-taking or trade settlement. The WFOE must maintain its regulated onshore account at a Tier-1 commercial bank and may use PayPal/Wise only as auxiliary disbursement pipes for cross-border panel incentives, funded by compliant onshore remittances. Any use must be supported by documented payout contracts, records of beneficial recipients, and service-trade filings to SAFE to avoid red flags.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Foreign statutory directors and the legal representative must typically attend an in-branch KYC interview at the receiving bank in mainland China. If the legal representative is physically abroad, banks will normally accept a notarized and consular- or apostille-authenticated power of attorney appointing an on-site senior manager, but that on-site representative must still appear before the compliance officer with the corporate chops, original passports, business licence, articles of association, UBO declarations, and a live video confirmation. Remote consular proxy opening is not unconditionally permitted; acceptance depends on the bank's risk policy and the completeness of the notarization chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and ownership chain opacity where an offshore holding company or nominee arrangement conceals the natural-person beneficial owner of the WFOE.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registry extract or certificate of incumbency for every entity in the ownership chain; passports and current proof of address of each natural-person shareholder/UBO with holdings above 25%; notarized Articles of Association and board resolutions; audited financial statements or proof of economic substance for the immediate overseas investor; sanctions, PEP and adverse-media screening report for all owners; certificate of legalization/apostille and Chinese consular authentication where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsupported or oversized inbound FDI remittance that exceeds the registered investment amount or lacks a clear SAFE capital-injection purpose code.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI foreign exchange registration notice issued by the receiving bank or local SAFE office; foreign investor's audited financial statements and 12-month bank statements demonstrating genuine source of funds; equity contribution agreement and WFOE shareholders' resolution; remittance instruction with the correct SAFE FDI capital contribution purpose code and reference to the registration number; board capital payment schedule; notarized loan/promissory note if the injection is part loan and part equity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mass cross-border payouts to overseas survey respondents through PayPal/Wise could be misconstrued as unauthorized money transmission or disguised service trade offshore.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements with the survey platform and foreign principals; itemized commercial invoices; detailed payout ledger with respondent unique identifiers, amounts, dates and currency; survey delivery evidence such as response datasets, timestamps and engagement logs; the payment aggregator's AML/KYC policy and transaction audit trail; SAFE service trade declaration forms and proof of tax withholding/declaration for any assessable payments; PIPL cross-border data transfer impact assessment or security filing if personal data is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical operational substance in mainland China, creating a shell-company typology.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly executed mainland office lease and rental invoices; social insurance and labor contract records for the WFOE's mainland employees; site photographs and utility bills; active corporate website and platform user agreements; minutes of board meetings held at the registered address; business plan and cash-flow projections consistent with the declared ISIC 7320 activity; China tax returns, VAT invoices and local business tax filings.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital is routed via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign investor's overseas bank to the WFOE's FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a Tier-1 Chinese bank. For RMB-denominated equity investment, the remittance can clear through CIPS. Prior to receipt, the WFOE must complete SAFE FDI foreign exchange registration, and the investor must reference the SAFE registration number and the approved capital contribution purpose code in the wire instruction. Upon receival, the bank verifies the amount against the registration, updates the SAFE monitoring system, and may credit the account. RMB settlement of the capital account is allowed for eligible operating uses, but prohibited for unauthorized securities investment, entrusted loans, non-operating real estate, or equity investments into other Chinese entities beyond legal limits. A licensed Chinese CPA must issue the capital verification report if required by the company's articles or the relevant approval authority.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the WFOE's service-trade disbursements, including consumer panel incentives and market-research vendor fees, the standard rail is a clean SWIFT MT103 remittance supported by a genuine contract, commercial invoice, proof of actual service delivery, tax withholding certificate where applicable, and a correct SAFE service-trade purpose code. RMB cross-border payments may be routed through CIPS, while foreign-currency payments use SWIFT. Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) and Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) are permissible only for goods-trade settlements, which may apply if the WFOE later imports equipment or merchandise; for ISIC 7320 services, wire remittance remains the dominant compliant rail. Bulk payouts to overseas respondents must be remitted from the onshore bank account to the licensed aggregator's settlement account under a documented payout arrangement, never as unstructured peer-to-peer transfers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts, permitted only when supported by genuine current-account trade or approved capital-account cash flow.
Onshore CNY/USD foreign exchange swaps, including spot/forward combinations, for daily operational liquidity and balance-sheet hedging.
Onshore cross-currency swaps or foreign currency interest rate swaps, permitted only if the underlying foreign-currency debt is registered with SAFE and used for approved capital-account purposes.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) and speculative derivative trades are not permitted for onshore entities; the WFOE must execute all hedging with a licensed onshore bank under the real-demand principle.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: National Enterprise Credit Information Annual Report (Enterprise Annual Report and business credit information publicity filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually January 1 to June 30 for the immediately preceding calendar year, filed by 23:59 Beijing time on June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or filing outside the window results in inclusion in the Enterprise List of Abnormal Operations; the default is published on the national credit information publicity system and the credit record of the legal representative may be restricted. Three consecutive years of non-filing triggers transfer to the Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List, after which SAMR may order correction and, if not corrected, initiate administrative strike-off or deregistration of the business license; an enterprise on the dishonesty list may also be barred from government procurement, investment incentives, and bank credit facilities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report under the Foreign Investment Law and Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the integrated annual report platform, with data transmitted to the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before June 30 for the preceding calendar year; the report captures the ultimate investment genealogy, shareholding percentages, WFOE operating status, and enterprise changes as of December 31 of the prior year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing the June 30 deadline or materially misreporting beneficial ownership is met with a written correction order, normally requiring rectification within 30 calendar days. If not cured, the foreign investor or WFOE is liable to an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000; the entity will also be posted to the Enterprise List of Abnormal Operations and may be barred from foreign-exchange registration changes until compliant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement (Annual CIT Filing and Tax Reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA), local competent tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by May 31 following the end of each calendar tax year; quarterly CIT prepayments are due by the 15th day after each quarter end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, and up to RMB 50,000 in serious cases; any unpaid tax balance accrues late-payment interest at 0.05% per day from the original due date until paid. Persistent non-filing permits the tax authority to freeze bank accounts, garnish receivables, block invoice issuance, and place the enterprise in the tax non-payment blacklist; the WFOE's business license may be revoked through co-enforcement with SAMR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and Chinese CPA Audit Report (where statutory audit threshold or regulator requirement is triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local SAMR credit information system, competent tax authority, shareholders meeting, and SAFE-regulated banks where foreign-exchange verification applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial statements must be prepared within four months after the December 31 balance sheet date; audited financial statements must be available no later than May 31 for CIT annual filing and before the SAMR annual report deadline of June 30; banks or offshore group accounts may impose a separately contracted deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to procure a statutory audit where required is a violation of PRC accounting and company law obligations and leaves the annual report unable to evidence solvency; SAMR may mark the filing abnormal, tax authorities may reject the tax settlement in certain cases, and lenders or investors may require accelerated repayment. Repeat failures can be treated as a refusal to maintain lawful books and records and may escalate to administrative revocation of the WFOE business license and disqualification of the legal representative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Insurance Contribution Base Declaration and Social Insurance Payment Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS) local social insurance bureau; local housing fund management center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the local MOHRSS notification period, generally May 15 through July 31 in major municipalities for the next contribution year; monthly contribution payments are due by the 15th day of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-declaration or late payment triggers statutory recovery and late-payment surcharge, plus an administrative fine of up to three times the unpaid amount under the PRC Social Insurance Law; continued non-compliance may lead to labor inspection enforcement, property preservation orders, restriction of the legal representative's exit from China, and, in aggravated cases, refusal by market regulation authorities to renew or continue the business license.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required when the WFOE exceeds any of the applicable PRC SME classification size thresholds at fiscal year-end: (i) balance-sheet total assets exceed RMB 40 million, (ii) annual operating revenue exceeds RMB 40 million, or (iii) average full-time headcount exceeds 300. Where all three figures are at or below the thresholds, the company may prepare financial statements under the Ministry of Finance Standards for Small Enterprises, but a statutory Chinese CPA audit remains mandatory if SAMR or MOFCOM foreign investment reporting, SAFE-registered foreign exchange approval banks, an offshore parent or lender, or the articles of association require audited statements. The audit must be a full-scope statutory audit under PRC China Auditing Standards (CAS) and may not be substituted with a review engagement or bookkeeper certification.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS), which are substantially converged with IFRS; micro and small enterprises may apply the Ministry of Finance Standards for Small Enterprises where eligible, but audited entities are expected to use full CAS. For offshore parent consolidation, a CAS-to-IFRS reconciliation workbook is normally required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must maintain a written beneficial ownership register and confirm the register annually with SAMR before June 30 each year, either through the national enterprise credit information annual report or the SAMR beneficial ownership database, whichever is in force. Any transfer of shareholding, change in direct or indirect shareholders, change in ultimate beneficial owner, change in voting

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday or special free-zone regime applies to a mainland China WFOE; qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises may enjoy a 15% rate; for 2023-2027 small low-profit enterprises with annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, taxable income is reduced by 25% and tax is then applied at 20%, producing an effective 5% preferential rate; qualifying R&D expenses may benefit from a 100% additional super deduction; the WFOE does not benefit from a patent box but market-research software development expenses may qualify for R&D deductions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: China Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000, supported by schedules A000000 (enterprise basic information), A105000 (tax adjustment items), A107010 (preferential income), A108000 (foreign tax credit), and A109000 (offshore income); quarterly provisional prepayment is made on Form A200000 through the China Tax Electronic Taxpayer portal (eTax) administered by the provincial State Taxation Administration bureau.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement return with quarterly provisional prepayments; quarterly returns are due within 15 days after each quarter-end and the annual final return is due within five months after the fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year WFOE, quarterly provisional CIT payments are due by April 15, July 15, October 15 and January 15 of the following year; the annual CIT return and any balance of tax must be filed and paid by May 31 of the year following the tax year; if the deadline falls on a statutory holiday or rest day, it extends to the next working day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from sales of goods, provision of services, and other business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must report all China-source and worldwide revenues; for cross-border consumer-panel SaaS clients, include subscription and market-research platform fees received from non-resident clients, converted into RMB using the applicable tax-period central parity rate; do not net-out panelist incentive payments, which are separate deductible costs subject to proper individual income tax withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of service delivery, data licences, cloud hosting, survey panel incentives, and direct labour.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All related-party charges from offshore affiliates must be arm’s length, contemporaneously documented, and supported by actual performance; otherwise the cost is disallowed under PRC transfer-pricing rules; panelist incentives paid to PRC individuals require payroll/IIT reporting, and defective contracts may recharacterise the payment as non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 3 - Sales and Marketing Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs directly incurred in acquiring survey respondents and consumer-panel enrolees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border marketing and respondent-acquisition fees paid to foreign related parties attract 10% withholding tax on China-source service income unless treaty relief is substantiated; payments to shell or no-substance service provider entities are red flags for GAAR recharacterisation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Head-office allocation, management fees, professional fees, software subscriptions, and general overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offshore parent management fees are deductible only to the extent actually incurred, arm’s length, and supported by evidence; excessive or notional management fees remitted abroad are recharacterised as non-deductible distributions and subject to 10% dividend withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 5 - Non-Operating Income and Non-Operating Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gains and losses outside ordinary operations, including asset disposals, claim settlements, and penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE is used as a pass-through for cross-border profit shifting, the tax authority may reclassify non-operating receipts as taxable ordinary income or deeme a dividend to the overseas shareholder; include full disclosure of China-sourced non-operating items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 6 - Total Profit before Tax Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit computed under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the audited financial statements to tax adjustment schedule A105000; the CNY functional currency books, audit report, and CIT return must be consistent because any unexplained mismatch invites an anti-fraud investigation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Line 7 - Taxable Income after Loss Carryforward and Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after adding back non-deductible items, applying tax exemptions, and utilising prior-year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the five-year loss carryforward only to verified tax losses; if the WFOE claims treaty benefits while reporting a constant zero or minimal taxable income, the special tax adjustment authorities will apply GAAR and adjust the profit allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Line 8 - Tax Payable at Applicable Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory tax payable before tax incentives and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute tax at 25% and reduce only for valid preferential rates and credits; a deemed dividend arising from an offshore indirect equity transfer is separately subject to 10% WHT and cannot be reduced in this box without proper filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for foreign income taxes paid on foreign-source income reported in the offshore income schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE may claim foreign tax credits only for taxes it actually bears on foreign-source profit; taxes paid by the overseas parent or affiliate are not creditable, and a double-dip credit claim creates a serious compliance red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 / Line 10 - Net CIT Payable or Overpayment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of annual settlement after quarterly provisional payments, prepayment credits, and prior refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Underpayment must be settled by May 31 or late-payment interest will accrue daily at 0.05%; overpayment can be refunded or carried forward but must be separately reconciled with the foreign-exchange repatriation records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return is punishable under Article 62 of the PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL) with a caution or fine up to RMB 2,000, rising to RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious cases; late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% under Article 32 TCAL; false returns or under-reported taxable income are sanctionable under Article 63 TCAL with a fine of 0.5 to 5 times the tax shortfall; criminal tax evasion under Article 201 of the Criminal Law arises where the evaded amount exceeds RMB 50,000 and is more than 10% of the total tax payable, carrying fines and imprisonment up to seven years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise shareholder under Articles 37 and 38 of the PRC CIT Law; a lower DTA rate is available if the shareholder is a treaty-resident and satisfies the beneficial-ownership test, generally 5% for direct shareholding of at least 25% or 10% in other holdings, but only after treaty relief is approved.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before any dividend distribution, the WFOE as withholding agent must collect: (i) a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign shareholder’s tax authority; (ii) a Treaty Benefit Application Form or Beneficial Owner Self-Declaration in the format required by SAT Announcements No. 35 of 2015 and No. 60 of 2018, filed through the eTax portal; (iii) evidence of ownership, substance, and board authorisation such as certificate of incumbency, share register, and financial statements; (iv) a declaration that the shareholder is not a conduit and has no obligation to pass the dividend to a third-country resident. The treaty benefit must be approved before or at the time of remittance; if approval is denied, the withholding agent must withhold at the 10% statutory rate and pay any shortfall with interest.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding tax rate is 10% for cross-border interest and royalties paid by a PRC resident enterprise to a non-resident (Article 37 CIT Law; Implementation Regulation Articles 90-105); treaty rates vary, commonly reducing interest to 7%-10% and royalties to 5%-10% depending on the DTA and type of intellectual property; intercompany software licence fees for survey algorithms, panel data, and market-research know-how are China-source royalties; related-party loans must respect the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin-capitalisation limit for non-financial enterprises, and interest in excess of the arm’s-length amount or debt-to-equity ratio is non-deductible and recharacterised as a deemed dividend subject to 10% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under SAT Announcement No. 42 of 2016, a Local File is mandatory for the WFOE if its related-party transactions in the prior tax year exceed RMB 200 million for tangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers, or RMB 40 million for related-party services and other transactions (including SaaS and market-research platform services); a Master File is triggered when annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion and a Country-by-Country Report is required when the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent reaches RMB 5.5 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime in the offshore-centre sense, but it applies substance-over-form under Article 47 CIT Law and SAT Announcement No. 2 of 2017; the WFOE must show real Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in China, including survey design, panel data collection, analytics, client contracting, pricing decisions, and support staff. If CIGA are performed by a foreign related entity without Chinese substance, the tax authority may reallocate residual profits to the WFOE, assess 25% CIT, add interest and surcharges, and impose 10% WHT on deemed distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fabricating survey-panel costs, using false offshore management-fee invoices, or channelling payments through PayPal/Wise to shell suppliers to reduce Chinese taxable profit, failing to report China-source market-research revenue, and intentionally maintaining false books to evade CIT and WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 TCAL requires recovery of the underpaid tax plus a fine of 50% to five times the tax shortfall; Article 201 Criminal Law criminalises evasion of RMB 50,000 or more exceeding 10% of the total tax payable, with fines and imprisonment up to seven years where the evaded amount is RMB 500,000 or more and exceeds 30% of the tax payable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Article 23 of the PRC Company Law (2023 revision) allows courts to pierce the corporate veil where a director abuses the limited-liability structure; the director becomes jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax and penalties, may face asset seizure and travel bans under civil enforcement blacklisting, and may be personally sentenced to imprisonment for up to seven years if found to have directed the false tax filings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and General Anti-Avoidance Rule
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the WFOE as an empty conduit with no Chinese employees, premises, or decision-making, shifting substantive consumer-survey and platform-IP activities to a zero-tax jurisdiction, or channelling royalties and service fees through a Hong Kong or Singapore mailbox company to obtain unintended DTA benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PRC GAAR under Article 47 CIT Law and SAT Announcement No. 2 of 2017 authorises tax authorities to disregard the shell, recharacterise the transactions, assess the reallocated profit at 25%, add late-payment interest plus an additional GAAR surcharge, and impose 10% withholding on deemed dividends; beneficial-ownership denial under the DTA strips any treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who structure a phantom WFOE to defeat tax liabilities are individually liable under civil enforcement rules and can be pierced under the Company Law; courts may recover tax penalties from personal assets, impose travel bans and high-consumption blacklisting, and refer criminal indictment under Article 201 Criminal Law for tax evasion or Article 208 for unlawful tax-invoice use, carrying imprisonment up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Foreign Exchange and AML Payment-Rail Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using PayPal Mass Payout or Wise to make cross-border payments to foreign survey respondents or related suppliers outside licensed SAFE channels, splitting payments to avoid transaction reporting, transferring undisclosed taxable profits through non-bank rails, or failing to register offshore equity and shareholder-loan transactions with SAFE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PRC Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations Articles 39 and 40 impose administrative fines of 30%-70% of the illegal foreign-exchange amount for unauthorised cross-border settlement and compulsory closure of unlawful channels; the revised Anti-Money Laundering Law of the PRC (2024) imposes penalties on payment institutions failing to implement suspicious-transaction reporting, including fines up to RMB 5 million and confiscation of illegal gains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly direct the WFOE to use non-compliant payment rails to hide taxable revenue or to bypass AML controls are personally exposed to SAFE fines, civil restitution through corporate-veil piercing, travel bans and asset restrictions, and criminal prosecution under Article 191 Criminal Law for money laundering, with fines and imprisonment up to ten years where the proceeds derive from tax evasion or fraud.
